exercises.title: U3 听力·对话 Ordering at a Chinese Restaurant
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: Waiter
transcript.text: Good evening. Would you like to order now?

transcript.speaker: Emma
transcript.text: Yes, please. It's my first time eating real Chinese food.

transcript.speaker: Waiter
transcript.text: Then let me suggest a few dishes. Do you like spicy food?

transcript.speaker: Emma
transcript.text: A little, but not too hot. I get scared of very spicy dishes.

transcript.speaker: Waiter
transcript.text: How about steamed fish and some fried rice with eggs?

transcript.speaker: Emma
transcript.text: That sounds lovely. Should I order rice for everyone?

transcript.speaker: Waiter
transcript.text: Yes. In China we usually share the dishes and each have our own bowl of rice.

transcript.speaker: Emma
transcript.text: I see. So everyone takes a little from each plate. What a nice custom!

exercises.translation_cn: Emma 第一次吃正宗中餐,请服务员推荐;服务员问她吃不吃辣,她说只能吃一点;服务员推荐清蒸鱼和蛋炒饭;并解释中餐通常是大家共享菜肴、各自一碗米饭。

questions.stem: Why does Emma ask the waiter for suggestions?
options: It is her first time eating real Chinese food.
She cannot read the menu at all.
She is in a hurry to leave.

questions.stem: How does Emma feel about spicy food?
options: She can eat only a little, not too hot.
She has never heard of it.

questions.stem: What two dishes does the waiter suggest?
options: Steamed fish and fried rice with eggs.

questions.stem: How are the dishes usually eaten in China, according to the waiter?
options: Each person orders one separate dish.
Everyone shares the dishes with their own bowl of rice.

questions.stem: What is Emma's reaction to the custom?
options: She wants to leave at once.
She thinks it is a nice custom.

exercises.title: U3 听力·短文 Dining Customs Around the World
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Every country has its own dining customs that may surprise a visitor.
In some places, it is rude to turn a fish over on the plate, because people believe it brings bad luck.
In China and Japan, you should never stand your chopsticks straight up in a bowl of rice.
In parts of the Middle East, people use only their right hand to touch food.
Learning these small rules before you travel shows respect for the local culture.
exercises.translation_cn: 每个国家都有自己的就餐习俗,常令游客吃惊;有的地方认为把鱼翻面会带来坏运气;在中国和日本,不要把筷子直插在米饭里;中东部分地区只用右手碰食物;出行前了解这些小规矩是对当地文化的尊重。

questions.stem: In some places, why should you not turn a fish over?
options: It makes the fish too cold.
The waiter has to clean it.
People believe it brings bad luck.

questions.stem: What should you never do with chopsticks in China and Japan?
options: Stand them straight up in a bowl of rice.
Hold them in your right hand.

questions.stem: In parts of the Middle East, which hand is used to touch food?
What is the main message of the passage?
options: All countries eat the same way.
Learning local rules shows respect for the culture.

questions.stem: Who might be surprised by these customs?

exercises.title: U3 听力·对话 A Question About Table Manners
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: I'm visiting a Chinese friend's home tomorrow. Any advice on table manners?

transcript.speaker: Lin
transcript.text: Sure. When you sit down, wait for the host to start the meal first.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Got it. And should I finish everything in my bowl?

transcript.speaker: Lin
transcript.text: Actually, if you finish it all, the host may think you want more food.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Really? At home I was taught to clean my plate to be polite.

transcript.speaker: Lin
transcript.text: Here it's the opposite. Leaving a little shows you are full and satisfied.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: That's so different! Anything else I should know?

transcript.speaker: Lin
transcript.text: Just relax and enjoy. They'll be happy that you try their food with an open mind.

exercises.translation_cn: Tom 明天去中国朋友家做客,向 Lin 请教餐桌礼仪;Lin 说要等主人先动筷;吃光碗里的饭主人会以为你还想要;在中国留一点反而表示吃饱了、满意了;最后建议他放松享受、以开放心态尝试。

questions.stem: Why does Tom ask Lin for advice?
options: He is visiting a Chinese friend's home.

questions.stem: What does Lin say to do when you sit down?
options: Wait for the host to start the meal first.

questions.stem: What might the host think if Tom finishes everything?
What does leaving a little food show in China?
options: That you are full and satisfied.

questions.stem: What is Lin's final piece of advice?
options: Relax and try the food with an open mind.

exercises.title: U3 听力·短文 Food and Childhood Memories
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Many of us connect our favourite foods with happy memories from childhood.
A single smell or taste can bring back a whole afternoon at our grandmother's table.
When we feel tired or sad as adults, we often look for these comfort foods.
They remind us of family, of home and of being cared for.
In this way, a simple dish can carry far more meaning than just a meal.
exercises.translation_cn: 我们许多人把最爱的食物与童年的快乐记忆相连;一种气味或味道就能唤回在奶奶餐桌旁的整个下午;长大后疲惫或难过时,我们常会寻找这些慰藉食物;它们让我们想起家人、家和被照顾的感觉;这样,一道简单的菜承载的意义远不止一顿饭。

questions.stem: What do many people connect their favourite foods with?
What can a single smell or taste bring back?
options: A whole afternoon at grandmother's table.

questions.stem: When do adults often look for comfort foods?
options: When they feel tired or sad.

questions.stem: What do these foods remind people of?
options: Family, home and being cared for.

questions.stem: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Cooking is a waste of time.
A simple dish can carry deep meaning.
Memories have nothing to do with food.

exercises.title: U3 听力·对话 Ordering Takeaway Food
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: Mia
transcript.text: I'm too tired to cook tonight. Shall we order some takeaway?

transcript.speaker: Jack
transcript.text: Good idea. What do you feel like eating?

transcript.speaker: Mia
transcript.text: Maybe something warm. How about noodle soup?

transcript.speaker: Jack
transcript.text: Sounds great. I'll get boiled dumplings too, with a little vinegar.

transcript.speaker: Mia
transcript.text: Perfect. Can you ask them to make mine less salty?

transcript.speaker: Jack
transcript.text: Sure. The shop near us has fresh, homemade noodles.

transcript.speaker: Mia
transcript.text: Lovely. How long will it take to arrive?

transcript.speaker: Jack
transcript.text: About thirty minutes. Let's set the table while we wait.

exercises.translation_cn: Mia 太累不想做饭,提议点外卖;Jack 同意,问她想吃什么;Mia 想吃热乎的面汤;Jack 还想点水煮饺子配点醋;Mia 请他让自己的少放盐;附近店有新鲜手工面;大约三十分钟送到,两人先摆好餐桌。

questions.stem: Why does Mia want to order takeaway?
options: She has no food at all.
She is too tired to cook.

questions.stem: What warm dish does Mia choose?
What does Jack want to order in addition?

exercises.title: U3 听力·短文 Eating a Balanced Meal
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: A good meal should be both nutritious and appealing to the eye.
Chinese cooks often try to balance many flavours in one meal.
They mix salty, spicy, sour, sweet and bitter tastes in a careful way.
A colourful plate of vegetables, meat and rice gives the body what it needs.
Eating a variety of fresh foods is one simple secret of staying healthy.
exercises.translation_cn: 一顿好饭应既有营养又赏心悦目;中国厨师常努力在一餐中平衡多种味道;把咸、辣、酸、甜、苦仔细调和;一盘色彩丰富的蔬菜、肉和米饭能给身体所需;吃多样的新鲜食物是保持健康的一个简单秘诀。

questions.stem: What should a good meal be, according to the passage?
options: Both nutritious and appealing to the eye.

questions.stem: What do Chinese cooks often try to balance?
Which five tastes are mentioned?
options: Hot, cold, warm, fresh and old.
Salty, spicy, sour, sweet and bitter.
Red, green, blue, white and black.
Big, small, long, short and round.

questions.stem: What gives the body what it needs?
options: A colourful plate of vegetables, meat and rice.

questions.stem: What is one simple secret of staying healthy?
options: Eating only one kind of food.
Eating a variety of fresh foods.
